# LightRAG patent evidence provenance
Time-limited validation record and statement of what was not completed

**Core result: the real index and QA with official LightRAG were not completed; it cannot be claimed that the experiment ran through.**
 Real data was obtained and verified, the official release was pinned, and its deterministic chunker was actually run. No configured and usable authorised LLM/embedding service was found in the current execution environment; the location of existing services was asked about, but no configuration was obtained. Under the constraint “do not keep spending time on environment problems”, the model stage was ended early, without waiting for or exceeding the 60/120-minute limits. No answer of this assistant was substituted for a model call, no mock model was used, and no paid service was signed up for.

**20** real English patents

**438** numbered claims

**48** actual official chunks

**0 / $0** model calls / new cost

## A. What was actually done

Run in a separate directory on this Mac; AutoDL was not accessed, and FOT, existing processes, model weights, tunnels and proxies were not modified. The data met the size and field requirements before 13:14:56 UTC, ahead of the 13:38:42 data gate. The official query gate was 14:08:42 and the overall deadline 15:08:42; this run stopped early because no model service was available, rather than continuing to try after the deadline.

Data source: [Dis2Pat](https://huggingface.co/datasets/lj408/Dis2Pat); only the first 100 rows of train were downloaded through the Dataset Viewer (about 6.75 MB). After deduplication by publication number, 20 patents on information retrieval, recommendation, contextual ranking and data indexing were selected purposively. The dataset revision recorded is `eda4a497291e9e8b898639881c34f158524732fc`; the raw API response and its SHA256 are kept. The sample is not random; no population error rate can be inferred.

Each input contains the complete original publication number, title, abstract and claims; the file name is the publication number. The specification is kept in the raw files but was not added to the chunking input this time; the generated disclosure is excluded completely. None of the 20 is truncated by the Viewer; all abstracts match Google Patents completely; the claims of 19/20 match completely after whitespace normalisation only. Anomalies: the parent claim numbers of US8509827B2 claims 2/3 are already missing on the source page; the formulas of US9218390B2 claims 10/11 are garbled by encoding. The original text was not rewritten; the test evidence avoids the affected content.

## C. The two most valuable cases observed

**There is no RAG QA success or failure case to report.** The following are actual data/chunking observations, not retrieval results and not model answers.

### Case 1: the cross-chunk assumption is refuted by the actual boundary

[US9514753B2](https://patents.google.com/patent/US9514753B2/en): the complete dependency chain claim 11→10→9→1 lies entirely within the same actual chunk 0 (chunks numbered from 0). Claim 1 concerns candidate speakers in hash tables; claim 10 introduces cosine distance; claim 11 requires the smallest cosine distance and the maximum distance threshold. In this configuration it cannot be said that this relation is lost across chunks. The boundary pre-check succeeded; extraction/retrieval/citation correctness remains untested.

### Case 2: real dependency evidence is naturally spread out, but no information loss has been shown yet

[US7991757B2](https://patents.google.com/patent/US7991757B2/en): the complete text of claim 1 lies in chunk 0, document character span [494,2433); the complete text of claim 27 lies in chunk 1, span [10570,10823). Claim 1 defines the registration module for external recommenders; claim 27 explicitly depends on claim 1 and adds the limitation machine readable descriptions of the external recommender. No chunk contains both complete claims, and the chunk boundaries were not adjusted artificially.

Claim 27 itself repeats the entity names and part of the relation, so the complete claims lying in different chunks does not by itself show an extraction failure. Attribution needs an actual check of the extraction output, graph nodes/edges, retrieval context and answer. A structural screen identified 364 explicit single-parent references, of which 54 pairs of complete claim texts do not share a chunk; this is a heuristic candidate count, **not 54 lost relations, still less an error rate**.

The problems that can be located clearly this time belong to the input data: missing parent claim numbers and garbled formula encoding. No defect of LightRAG's extraction, indexing, retrieval, generation or citation was confirmed.

## D. Research judgments and version limits

| Research question | What this run can support |
| ---|--- |
| Document-level provenance? | The current release's source provides a file_paths→reference_id document mapping; naive is text-chunk retrieval, mix combines entities, relations and text chunks. There is no run evidence yet to judge the actual accuracy of the citations in answers. |
| Reliable claim-level provenance? | Not verified yet. The current formatted query result contains chunk_id/content/file_path/reference_id, with no explicit claim ID or character offsets; the internal chunker/pipeline already supports source spans, so it cannot be said that the system has no span provenance at all. The existence of a document citation also does not mean that the answer is entailed by a claim. |
| Reproduce cross-chunk relation loss? | No. The natural separation of claim evidence was reproduced, and two initial cross-chunk candidates were refuted; without intermediate results of extraction/graph/retrieval/generation, no relation loss can be attributed. |
| Defect or experimental limitation? | Confirmed are data-quality problems, the granularity of the returned schema, and the absence of a model service this time; no current code defect was confirmed. Incremental insertion was not executed, so merge consistency cannot be judged. |
| Questions worth pursuing? | Evidence organisation aware of claim dependencies; keeping verifiable original-text spans for entities/relations/answers; measuring fact retention stage by stage; explicitly separating facts from inferences in cross-document comparisons; source consistency after incremental entity merging. These are research directions to be verified, not defects shown in this run. |

Interface check: `aquery_llm` can save the answer and entities/relationships/chunks/references in the same call; `/query/data` calls `aquery_data`, which generates no answer but may still need the keyword model and embedding. The core `QueryParam.include_references` defaults to false, REST to true; `include_chunk_content` is a REST parameter and must not be passed to QueryParam by mistake.

The paper [v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.05779v3) is dated 2025-04-28 and Figure 1 already shows raw chunk IDs; the current README records citations under 2025-03. It cannot be claimed that the paper-era version had no citation feature at all. This run uses the 2026 release code, does not reproduce a fixed artifact of the paper period, and does not project current behaviour back onto the paper.

Source basis: [formatted chunks and document references](https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/28ff1b05f2ac3f3e6fa14dd2cd33656579bd0c9c/lightrag/utils.py#L6936); [REST parameters](https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/28ff1b05f2ac3f3e6fa14dd2cd33656579bd0c9c/lightrag/api/routers/query_routes.py#L144); [official chunker](https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/28ff1b05f2ac3f3e6fa14dd2cd33656579bd0c9c/lightrag/chunker/token_size.py#L133); [official release record](https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/releases/tag/v1.5.7). Line numbers, source excerpts and hashes item by item in evidence/official_stable_audit.json.

## Review and file list

Open evidence/question_ground_truth.txt to check the original text question by question; naive/mix are null in results/questions.json; results/chunk_probe.json keeps all actual chunks; results/question_chunk_mapping.json and natural_cross_chunk_candidates.json record the boundary mapping; data/manifest.json, source_verification.json and data_quality_flags.json record the sampling and the comparison with the source pages.

The source archive is evidence/official_LightRAG_v1.5.7_source.tar.gz, the dependency list evidence/requirements_installed.json. The scripts scripts/data_*.py reproduce the data process; scripts/chunk_probe.py imports the pinned release source directly with a 30-second run limit; scripts/build_questions.py and map_question_chunks.py allow the evidence to be rechecked. No model process ran, and there is no background model/training task. No API request is left pending payment or with an uncertain result.
